clue.text: Comment by mail showing army's advanced viewpoint

parts.note: a comment or remark is an observation
sent by mail means sent by post

explanation.surface: A remark sent through the mail reveals where the army keeps watch from.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward position from which soldiers watch enemy movements is exactly this military lookout.

clue.text: Person in authority is in charge, guarded by volunteer

indicators.note: something guarded by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to volunteer is to offer

explanation.surface: A boss is in charge while being protected by a volunteer.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer holds a position of command or authority, in the forces or an organisation.

clue.text: Number of partners capturing first offender

indicators.note: the partners capturing something hold it between them, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: in bridge South and North are partners, abbreviated S and N
Eve, who ate the forbidden fruit, was the first sinner in Genesis

explanation.surface: A count of couples who have caught someone committing their first crime.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players North and South are a partnership, so 'partners' gives S and N, which go round EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a cardinal number, the one after six.

clue.text: Short, simple song — any louder ruins it

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are ruined, wrecked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gentle little song is spoilt if anyone sings it louder.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short simple song with a recurring refrain, an old lyric form.

clue.text: Operatic part Callas at first rejected

indicators.note: the opening letter of the singer's first name is thrown out

parts.note: Maria Callas was the famous Greek-American operatic soprano

explanation.surface: Maria Callas turned down a role in an opera at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Callas' stands for her first name MARIA; losing its first letter M leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song within an opera, a part sung by one voice.

clue.text: One quarter left in New York — that's not fair

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: these pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: E, for east, is one of the four compass quarters
left, as in departed, means quit

explanation.surface: Someone protests at being one of a quarter of the population left behind in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' is a compass point, E (east), not a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequity means unfairness or injustice, the condition of something not being fair.

clue.text: Country's north-east hearing apostle

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard spoken, a word given by its sound

parts.note: Paul was the apostle to the Gentiles

explanation.surface: A nation's north-eastern region is listening to a saint preach.
explanation.walkthrough: PAL is spoken just like PAUL, the apostle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country lying between India and China.

clue.text: Traditional group that has no small fry in it?

definitions.text: Traditional group that has no small fry in it?

parts.words: Traditional group that has no small fry in it?
parts.note: a shoal of fish in which none is a young fry would be a school of elderly fish, and the phrase also means traditional

explanation.surface: A conservative club that admits nobody unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: A school is a group of fish, and fry are young fish; a school with no youngsters is all old.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes conservative, traditional attitudes or methods, and literally an aged shoal of fish.

clue.text: As part of deal, exchange low grades in school

indicators.note: the grades are placed inside the verb for school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
D and E are low marks on a grading scale

explanation.surface: A school swaps over to poor marks as part of an arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over in exchange as part payment towards a new one.

clue.text: Peculiar virtue of a royal confidant

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the following letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A king's trusted adviser shows a strange kind of virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite is a monarch's intimate companion, often a court adviser with great influence.

clue.text: Help old passengers initially going wrong way for platforms

indicators.note: the run of pieces is read backwards, travelling the wrong direction

parts.note: to help is to aid

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Assisting elderly travellers who head off the wrong way to find their station platforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong way' turns AIDOP (AID, O and the P of passengers) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia is a plural of podium, a raised platform for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: Country area linked with each part of peace group

parts.note: CND is the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, a British peace movement, taken here a letter at a time
the second letter of CND
A again, joined to the next letter
the third letter of CND
A once more, joined to the last letter

explanation.surface: A nation with territory linked to every faction of a pacifist organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: CND is the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, a British peace movement. 'each part' means an A (area) follows each of its three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is the North American country north of the United States.

clue.text: Embellishment of part of billiard sharp's punishment, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is given by its sound, spoken not spelt

parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado the billiard sharp is condemned to play with a twisted cue, a bendy one

explanation.surface: A decorative flourish is part of the penalty for cheating at billiards.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado's song 'A more humane Mikado', the billiard sharp must play 'with a twisted cue', so a curly cue is part of his punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A curlicue is a decorative twist or curl, a flourish in handwriting or ornament.

clue.text: It can be an expression of protest, in fact

definitions.text: It can be an expression of protest
definitions.meaning: an indignant exclamation, like 'honestly!', used to object
meaning actually or truly, as an adverb

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an exclamation of disapproval and also as an adverb meaning actually.

clue.text: High-scoring fifteen —- as needed for optimal break

definitions.meaning: the New Zealand national rugby union team, a side of fifteen players known for running up big scores
the maximum break in snooker, 147, requires the black to be potted after every red

explanation.walkthrough: The ALL BLACKS are New Zealand's rugby union side; in snooker a maximum 147 break takes fifteen reds each followed by the black.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand rugby team carry this nickname, and a maximum snooker break means potting every black possible.

clue.text: What can make a strong handle, primarily?

definitions.text: What can make a strong handle, primarily?

indicators.note: the following letters can be made into something else, rearranged
only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Asking what material would make a sturdy handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges A STRONG with H, the first letter of handle; the whole clue also defines, since antler is used for knife handles.
explanation.definitionFit: Staghorn, the antler of a deer, is a tough material traditionally used for knife and walking-stick handles.

clue.text: Unpleasant type locked up in prison, one in part of Turkey

indicators.note: something locked up in a prison is held inside it

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pill is slang for a tiresome, disagreeable person
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A nasty character is imprisoned, a man held in a region of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: PILL as an unpleasant or tiresome person is informal, chiefly American; 'up' signals reading it upwards because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli is a peninsula in north-west Turkey, scene of the 1915 campaign.

clue.text: Motorist carrying old merrymaker

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: a motorist is a car user

explanation.surface: A driver gives a lift to an elderly reveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who drinks and revels noisily, a merrymaker.

clue.text: Preserve put by boy in cooking pot

indicators.note: put by means placed beside, so the preserve goes next to the boy

parts.note: Billy is a boy's name
to preserve food is to can it

explanation.surface: Jam is stored beside a lad in a saucepan.
explanation.walkthrough: A BILLYCAN is a camper's metal pot used over a fire, common in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal cooking pot with a lid and wire handle used for camping.

clue.text: Report about ruddy tedious state

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, a boom
ruddy means red in colour

explanation.surface: A news report about a bloody boring situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruddy' looks like the British mild swearword, but here it is the colour red.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the weary state of being uninterested and finding things tedious.

clue.text: Go downhill fast, certainly not going straight

definitions.text: Go downhill fast, certainly not going straight

parts.words: Go downhill fast, certainly not going straight
parts.note: describes racing down a ski slope while zigzagging between gates

explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a ski race weaving through a course of gates, and to slalom is to ski such a course.

clue.text: Chap upset about rook that may be seen atop French house

definitions.text: that may be seen atop French house

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: upset means sad
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A man is unhappy about a bird perched on top of a house in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is just SAD. A mansard roof is named after the French architect François Mansart.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansard is a roof with a steep lower slope, typical of French buildings.

clue.text: Belief left one, in part

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the word for part

parts.note: a part of a country is a region
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A faith abandoned by one person, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of faith and belief.

clue.text: Keep tight hold on king cobra

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
an asp is a type of venomous snake, here standing for cobra

explanation.surface: A monarch holds tightly onto a deadly snake.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is Georgius Rex, seen on British postboxes. The asp, Cleopatra's snake, is often identified with the Egyptian cobra.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to seize it and keep a firm hold of it.

clue.text: Scanty clothing being worn as underling

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A subordinate wearing very skimpy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a servile subordinate, a follower who does menial work.

clue.text: Namely, what's central to inside story

indicators.note: only the central letters of the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: Specifically, what lies at the heart of the insider's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the middle of 'inside story', spanning the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est, Latin for 'that is', means namely, abbreviated i.e.

clue.text: This part of fastening device isn't quite bust?

parts.note: someone who still has something is not entirely broke
P is a penny, the last coin left to someone almost broke

explanation.surface: Asking whether this bit of a lock is very nearly broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like broken, but it means penniless: someone who has P (a penny) isn't quite bust.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is the hinged metal strap of a fastening that fits over a staple and is secured by a padlock.

clue.text: A hard scoundrel returned home in Russia

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A tough villain came back to his house in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses AHCAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or villa.

clue.text: Thus a poet and artist combined to make serial for TV

parts.note: thus means so
Alexander Pope was an English poet
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A poet and a painter collaborate on a television series.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running television drama serial about everyday lives.

clue.text: Stole is fitting for occasion in Maryland

indicators.note: these words are placed within the abbreviation of the state

parts.note: MD is the abbreviation for the US state of Maryland
suitable for the occasion means appropriate

explanation.surface: A scarf is suitable for an event in Maryland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a wrap or scarf, but it is the past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To misappropriate is to take dishonestly for one's own use, so stole means misappropriated.
